match.reason: No bank point covers the full macro environment: the closest cards each cover only some factors (economic, social and technological in an HR context, or social, legal and political), and none covers global factors, so the new point is broader than any of them.

draft.title: The macro environment
card: The macro environment is the set of wide forces that affect all businesses in a country or region. A single business cannot influence them.
the state of the economy, such as the level of employment and what people can afford to spend.
the decisions of governments and the laws that businesses must follow.
social factors are the values and habits of society. Technological factors are new tools and ways of doing things. Global factors are events and trends overseas that reach businesses at home.
draft.remember: Macro forces are wide, shared by many businesses and beyond one business's control.

a.q: Which of these is part of the macro environment for a new bakery in Ballarat?
opts: A new law that changes the rules for food labels
The price the bakery chooses for its sourdough loaf
The recipe the bakery uses for its meat pies
The roster the owner sets for the bakery's staff
a.why: A law is made by government and applies to many businesses. The bakery cannot change it. The price, the recipe and the roster are all decisions the owner makes, so they are not macro forces.
a.clue: Which one is a wide force that the owner cannot change?

b.q: Nina plans a bike repair shop in Geelong. She is told that more people are choosing to cycle to work. Which macro factor is this?
opts: A social factor, as it is a change in how people live
A legal factor, as it is a change in the rules for riders
A political factor, as it is a decision made by government
A technological factor, as it is a change in the tools used
b.why: People choosing to cycle is a shift in the habits of society, so it is a social factor. It is tempting to call it a legal or political factor, but the card links those to laws and government decisions, and none are described here.
b.clue: Think about who is making the change: the government, or people in society?

a.best: A new law that changes the rules for food labels

b.best: A social factor, as it is a change in how people live
